title: minimal-event-fragment-schema-and-actor-enrichment-protocol
creator: Priya Kapoor
description: Scope: define a compact, index-friendly 'event fragment' schema for admin-facing audit events and a lightweight actor enrichment protocol that links SSO/SAML session metadata to audit records. Goals: reduce per-event storage footprint, improve query performance for actor/target inquiry patterns, preserve complete change intent for compliance use cases, and provide deterministic deserializers for the Console and external compliance exports. This ticket standardizes what fields must appear in minimal fragments, how to represent deltas for complex resources (maps, lists, role sets), and how to attach SAML/SSO session anchors without duplicating large identity blobs.
background: Current audit logs contain full snapshots for many admin operations which inflates storage and slows queries. Multiple teams have implemented ad-hoc diff encodings that are opaque to the Console; SSO session linkage is stored inconsistently (sometimes as full SAML assertions, sometimes as ephemeral session IDs). This causes difficulty for fast forensic queries and leads to retention cost spikes. We need a single minimal fragment schema + an enrichment pointer pattern to decouple identity material from the core event payload while retaining strong linkage and integrity guarantees.
acceptance_criteria: Define a 10-field maximal minimal-event-fragment that captures verb, resource_type, resource_id, canonical_change_token, timestamp, actor_ref, outcome, severity, truncated_diff, and meta_flags
Delta encoding: provide canonical serialized forms for add/remove/replace on maps and lists with deterministic ordering and a concise path notation
Actor enrichment protocol: specify actor_ref scheme (actor_hash), enrichment pointers to ID bundles stored in a separate 'identity-bag' service, and signed session anchors for SSO/SAML linkage
Backward-compatible ingestion: existing audit producers can emit full snapshots or the new fragment; ingestion pipeline must normalize both into the canonical fragment+enrichment layout
Console and compliance exports can reconstruct a human-readable before/after view from fragment + enrichment within 300ms for common queries
Storage savings: average per-admin-event stored size reduced by >=40% in staging bucket after rollout (measured with representative week)
tasks: Draft canonical minimal-event-fragment JSON schema and path notation spec
Design enrichment pointer API and storage contract for identity-bag service
Implement producer-side helpers (Go/Python libs) for fragmentization and diff generation
Update ingestion normalization job to accept both full snapshots and fragments and emit canonical envelope
Add Console deserializer and renderer for fragment+enrichment to show before/after diffs
Create migration job to compact recent 90-day admin events into fragment+pointer layout
Run storage-savings experiment in staging and produce dashboard metrics
Prepare operational runbook for failed enrichment resolution and fallbacks
technical_notes: Fragment design favors stable short keys (e.g., 'rt' for resource_type) to minimize on-disk size and improve compression
Delta notation uses JSON Pointer-like paths with numeric indexes for lists and ':+', ':-' for list add/remove operations
Actor hashing uses sha256(tenant_id + actor_scope + stable_actor_id) truncated to 16 bytes and base64url encoded; identity-bag holds full identity blobs and SAML assertion metadata
Enrichment pointers include a signed anchor: {pointer_id, issued_at, signer_key_id, signature} to prevent tampering when resolving historical events
Retention classes: 'ephemeral' (30d), 'standard' (365d), 'compliance' (7y) must be supported via per-event meta_flags
Indexing: primary indexes will be (tenant_id, resource_type, resource_id) and secondary on actor_hash and canonical_change_token
Ingestion should attach a small 'repair token' when enrichment fails to allow async backfill without blocking event persistence
migration_plan: Phase 1: Accept-only - deploy ingestion normalization that understands fragment+enrichment and full snapshots, and emits canonical envelope to new topic
Phase 2: Producers opt-in - ship helper libs and adapt top consumers (console, admin microservices) to emit fragments for new admin flows
Phase 3: Backfill - run compact job to re-encode last 90 days of admin snapshot events into fragments and create enrichment pointers; validate via checksum-based sampling
Phase 4: Hard cutover - mark legacy snapshot format deprecated, enable storage tiering that prefers fragments for cold storage
Phase 5: Observability - monitor 'enrichment-miss-rate', average event size, query latency, and runbook incident exercises
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: enrichment pointer TTLs could expire and break historical reconstruction - Mitigation: include archived identity-bag snapshots for compliance-class events
Risk: producers may generate non-deterministic diffs - Mitigation: provide a reference library and unit tests, require CI linting that validates deterministic ordering
Risk: additional complexity in Console deserialization - Mitigation: build shared server-side renderer that returns reconstructed before/after blobs to the Console
Risk: increased latency on first enrichment resolution - Mitigation: cache common identity-bag entries in the ingestion layer and pre-warm for high-volume actors
